answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity capital locked before an agent acts: each new account posts a bond that stays frozen while it operates, slashed if caught running as a duplicate of another. Honest agents show commitment with copper-grade collateral, small and liquid, while serious operators stake ferrous-grade reserves that stay costly at scale. A thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand bonds at once, so attack cost grows linearly while each fake earns nothing. The registry is a crystal ledger: every bond and slash is public.
